classification.difficultyReason: Use scaffolded vertical triangles to derive ground distances, then apply the bearing angle in cosine rule.

content.prompt:
From two points $P$ and $Q$ on level ground, the angles of elevation of the top $T$ of a 38 m tower are $26^\circ$ and $22^\circ$ respectively.

Point $P$ is due south of the tower, and the bearing of $Q$ from the tower is $100^\circ\mathrm{T}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 18, perspective tower diagram below part b
spec.description: Perspective triangle PTQ with internal ground point B directly below T. TP, TQ and PQ are solid; TB, PB and BQ are dashed. PB continues through B to a dashed north arrow. Cyan sectors mark the elevations at P and Q and the bearing between BN and BQ. Preserve the right-angle marker at B, the curved 38 m leader to TB and the curved 100° leader to the bearing sector.
spec.mathematics: TB=38 m; angle TPB=26°; angle TQB=22°; P is due south of B; Q has bearing 100°T from B. TB is perpendicular to the ground plane. The projected sector is not a plan-view measurement of the bearing.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $PB=38\tan64^\circ$, and find a similar expression for $QB$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence determine, correct to the nearest metre, the distance between $P$ and $Q$.
